sentence: This project uses single cell sequencing of early diabetic kidney samples to find the cell types and pathways that contribute to disease progression.
This project builds computational methods based on deep learning to find changes in microbial proteins and sugars in inflammatory bowel disease.
This project develops a bladder organ chip with sensors to model and study how the human bladder ages.
This project develops mass spectrometry techniques to study the structures of integral membrane proteins in their native membranes and tissues.
This project studies how bone stem cells work in mouse models of osteogenesis imperfecta and how bone healing could improve.
This project tries to find out how fucosyltransferases regulate immunity in mucosal epithelial tissues and builds a toolkit to reveal their substrates.
This project builds a computer model of the lower urinary tract that combines mathematical models with artificial intelligence to study nerve stimulation.
This project isolates endothelial cells from mice and human tissue and studies their metabolism, inflammation and barrier function.
This project uses a spinning disc confocal microscope to image research on brain development, cancer and reproductive health.
This project tries to find targets that protect the heart from arrhythmia caused by the drug ibrutinib, using cardiomyocytes and a mouse model.
This project uses sequencing to profile microbial composition and gene activity in fecal, blood and breastmilk samples.
This project develops statistical and artificial intelligence tools to explain why some people stay cognitively sharp despite high pathology for Alzheimer's disease.
This project develops an ultrasound imaging method that uses the drug hydralazine to make hepatocellular carcinoma easier to see early.
This project tries to identify genes in the gut microbiome that improve response to cancer immunotherapy and tests them as treatments.
This project studies whether glycolysis in red blood cells could be a target for drugs against malaria parasites.
This project tries to find out how defective DNA repair in trophoblast leads to placental injury in preeclampsia.
This project tests whether combining inhibitors of glutaminase and aldehyde dehydrogenase can kill cells of relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.
This project studies how oligodendrocytes respond to harmful stimuli, how to protect them, and how lost myelin can be replaced.
This project builds a method that links when neurons are born to their transcriptomic profiles, and applies it to human retinal organoids.
This project builds a framework that uses mathematical decision science modeling to judge how algorithms affect health care before they are deployed.
